applies_why: Yes: the judge decides the D5/C5 collision by noting that [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows and then leaving the sign's sense open, which is a row-level disposition rather than a chain-against-chain footing analysis.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: never verse by verse — reading one: it bars only deciding by isolated single verses, so separate named rows might be allowed; reading two: it bars deciding by separately argued scriptural rows when those rows are the pressing side's own chain, requiring chain-against-chain footing.
why: Because the judge's stated reason evaluates separate 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows and whether the sign's sense is open, not the relative footing of the two chains, it breaches K-C.
